accepted_units.title: Different regularizations expose different gauge presentations of one theory
accepted_units.why_material: The source isolates a reusable comparison principle: changes in contact-term regularization can change the manifest symmetry and field variables while preserving the underlying theory, so the descriptions must be related by a field redefinition.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument is presented in a worldsheet gauge-theory setting and does not establish a regulator-independent theorem for arbitrary mathematical systems. It supports representation-change reasoning, not a claim that every pair of presentations is equivalent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Pauli-Villars variables expose ordinary gauge symmetry and the invariant combination B+F, whereas point splitting exposes a noncommutative star-product gauge symmetry. PDF extraction is readable here, but symbols and line breaks should be checked against the source image before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Preserve equivalence classes without identifying their generating groups
accepted_units.why_material: An abelian/nonabelian obstruction rules out group isomorphism, after which the source identifies the weaker sufficient target: a field-dependent map preserving the gauge-equivalence relation. This is a generic distinction between presentation-level generators and quotient-level structure.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction is asserted only order by order in the deformation parameter; the source explicitly warns that the nonperturbative map may fail through nonconvergence. The gauge-theory example supplies the mechanism but does not make it universal.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The map of gauge parameters depends on both the original parameter and field, so it identifies equivalence relations rather than defining a homomorphism between the ordinary and noncommutative gauge groups.

accepted_units.title: Generate a change of variables by differential transport in the deformation parameter
accepted_units.why_material: The source turns a first-order compatibility calculation into a differential equation transporting fields and parameters between nearby associative products, yielding a systematic all-finite-orders construction.
accepted_units.context_note: All-finite-orders is formal perturbative control, not convergence or a global nonperturbative equivalence; the source explicitly places convergence beyond scope. Formula extraction is dense and must be source-verified before exact symbolic use.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The transport uses the explicit star-product family and its associativity; changing the deformation product or coordinate conventions can change the displayed map while retaining the quotient-preservation goal.

accepted_units.title: Poles delimit where one representation ceases to exist
accepted_units.why_material: Solving the transport for constant curvature exposes reciprocal formulas whose poles distinguish failure of the noncommutative chart from failure of the commutative chart. This is a reusable warning that an equivalence map can be locally meaningful while individual representations have different domains.
accepted_units.context_note: The demonstration is a rank-one constant-curvature special case. A pole is evidence of description breakdown, not by itself evidence that the underlying object or theory is singular.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The singular sets depend on which of F or its transformed counterpart is used as coordinate; only the invariant combination B+F explains the boundary in the ordinary presentation.

accepted_units.title: Recombine presentation-dependent variables into a background-invariant object
accepted_units.why_material: By separating background change from regulator change, replacing derivative-bearing coordinates with an abstract fixed-rank algebra, and holding local-frame components fixed, the source constructs invariant combinations of curvature and deformation data.
accepted_units.context_note: The core construction initially assumes invertible deformation tensor and fixed closed metric, and it is motivated within noncommutative gauge theory. Equations are formula-dense and require source-level verification before materialization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Curvature and the deformation tensor separately vary with the background split, while the commutator form and Q=theta Fhat theta-theta remain fixed under the specified change; this invariance depends on the chosen abstract-algebra and local-frame identification.

accepted_units.title: Preserving an action propagates invariance requirements to measures, couplings, rank, and center
accepted_units.why_material: The source shows that invariance of an integrand is insufficient: the integration measure forces a coupling transformation, while degeneracy of the deformation tensor restricts admissible changes to those preserving rank and algebraic center.
accepted_units.context_note: The transformation law is derived in a specific action and torus/noncommutative-space setting. It should be reused as a structural pattern—propagate an invariance demand through all dependent data—not as a domain-free formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The allowed background variation depends on whether theta is invertible. When it is degenerate, central coordinates and rank become structural data that the comparison must preserve.

accepted_units.title: State equivalence only modulo total derivatives and omitted derivative terms
accepted_units.why_material: The source gives an explicit proof pattern for comparing two actions: specify the approximation, vary a deformation parameter at fixed underlying data, integrate by parts, and conclude equality only modulo total derivatives and terms excluded by the approximation.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a slowly-varying rank-one DBI calculation, not an exact equality of local Lagrangians or a general proof of the proposed arbitrary-deformation description. OCR damage in matrix formulas makes exact algebra high risk without checking the typeset source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: One presentation packages deformation in a star product and transformed field, while the other uses ordinary fields and B+F. The equivalence depends on discarding derivative corrections consistently in both representations.

accepted_units.title: A moduli space can forget parameters retained by its representatives
accepted_units.why_material: The source separates dependence of the classified moduli space on a parameter combination from dependence of individual solutions on the full parameter pair because their coefficient algebra still changes. This is a strong generic example of quotienting forgetting information that representatives retain.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument specializes the noncommutative ADHM construction and explicitly builds on cited prior work; independent novelty is unconfirmed. The physical instanton interpretation is not required for the quotient-versus-representative distinction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The moduli equations depend only on the sum of two deformation components, but the algebra in which each connection takes values depends on both, obstructing direct comparison of representatives across parameter choices.

accepted_units.title: Disambiguate same-space field redefinition from space-changing duality
accepted_units.why_material: The source tracks the domain of a fractional transformation, identifies rational cases that become commutative, records singular group elements, and then distinguishes this duality from a different change of variables that leaves the space and rank fixed.
accepted_units.context_note: The transformation laws arise from torus T-duality and are formula-sensitive. The reusable content is the explicit comparison of what each equivalence preserves, changes, and where it becomes singular; it does not establish a new general duality family.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The field redefinition works for arbitrary deformation on the same torus and rank but complicates the action; the rational duality changes torus volume and rank while mapping a simple action to another simple action. Singular transformations restrict the effective action of the nominal duality group.

accepted_units.title: Two commuting actions induce left-right bimodule structure
accepted_units.why_material: The source makes the bimodule mechanism concrete: operators acting at opposite boundaries commute, orientation reverses multiplication on one side, and ground states therefore carry compatible left and right actions. Varying one boundary produces a family of modules.
accepted_units.context_note: The realization uses open-string boundary states and a zero-slope limit; the algebraic conclusion is generic, but the physical construction is only one source of commuting actions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Choosing one endpoint as left and the other as right determines the action conventions; reversing the boundary orientation replaces the product by its opposite, which is essential rather than superficial notation.

accepted_units.title: Stable complementation yields projective modules with topological invariants
accepted_units.why_material: The source connects the stable-complement definition of a projective module to sections of bundles, then transports projectivity to the noncommutative construction and separates ordinary Chern-class data from a deformation-dependent Chern character.
accepted_units.context_note: These are standard mathematical facts used by the source, not novel results, and one exceptional boundary-condition case is handled through an associated K-theory element rather than a bundle.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The same module may be encoded by a bundle, a K-theory class, or a noncommutative module; the source warns that their associated invariants are related but not identical.

accepted_units.title: Bimodules and balanced tensor products transport module and connection data
accepted_units.why_material: The source identifies mutual commutants, constructs the Morita correspondence by tensoring with an inter-algebra bimodule, explains composition through associativity, and shows how shared right-end data transports connections and gauge theories between algebras.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof is presented through a physical boundary-state realization and cites mathematical results for the torus duality identification. The Morita mechanism is source-grounded, but novelty relative to the parent corpus remains unassessed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Selecting one endpoint algebra as the geometric space or instead fixing it while acting on its commutant yields different descriptions of the same transported module data; the balanced tensor product removes the intermediate algebra action.

ecosystem_findings.summary: The source repeatedly separates invariant or quotient-level content from regulator-, coordinate-, background-, and representative-dependent descriptions, while recording approximation and domain boundaries. This supports the assignment-proposed lens; novelty relative to #44 was not checked.

The source supplies concrete duality objects—bimodules, commutants, balanced tensor products, projective modules—and explicit constraints on rank, center, measure, and transformation domain. This reinforces the assignment-proposed lens without asserting a new family or independent mathematical novelty.

inspection_summary: All 4,808 logical lines were inspected. The source contains high-value generic mechanisms around quotient preservation, deformation transport, invariants, approximation-aware equivalence, moduli versus representatives, and Morita transport. Selection is conservative because the document is primarily theoretical physics, many derivations are formula-dense, and PDF extraction damages spacing, glyphs, accents, and equation layout. Explicit conjectures, unsupported extensions, and physical compactification arguments were not promoted to units. Novelty and duplication relative to the frozen parent corpus remain unconfirmed.
